title: Subduction: slab-pull, trench and volcanic arc
subject: geography

scenes.caption: Two plates converge over the ocean
scenes.narration: At a convergent boundary an oceanic plate and a continental plate move towards each other. The oceanic plate is denser.

shape.explain: Mantle: the hot, slowly flowing rock beneath the plates.
Ocean: the sea sitting above the oceanic plate.
Oceanic plate: thin but dense rock, so it sits lower.
Continental plate: thicker but lighter rock, so it rides higher.
Label: the oceanic plate, the denser of the two.
Label: the continental plate.
Convergence arrow: the plates move towards each other.

steps.text: The two plates converge — the denser one will give way

scenes.caption: The denser plate bends down at the trench
scenes.narration: Too dense to stay afloat, the leading edge of the oceanic plate bends downwards. The deep fold where it dives is the ocean trench.

shape.explain: Mantle: the hot rock the slab will sink into.
Ocean: deepest right above the trench.
Continental plate: it stays on top at this boundary.
Oceanic plate: still flat where it approaches the trench.
The slab: the bent-down leading edge of the oceanic plate, diving into the mantle.
Ocean trench: the deep fold where the plate bends down.
Label: the ocean trench.
Label: the sinking slab.
Gravity arrow: the cold, dense slab is pulled downwards.

steps.text: Too dense to float, the oceanic plate bends down and sinks

scenes.caption: Slab-pull drags the plate; earthquakes track the slab
scenes.narration: The sinking slab is heavy, so gravity pulls it down and it drags the rest of the plate behind it — slab-pull. As the slab cracks and grinds downwards, earthquakes fire along its path.

shape.explain: Mantle: the slab sinks deeper into it.
Ocean: above the trench.
Continental plate: overriding plate at the boundary.
The slab: deeper now, still sinking under its own weight.
Trailing oceanic plate: being dragged towards the trench by the slab.
Label: earthquakes follow the slab down.
Slab-pull arrow: the sinking slab drags the plate down and along.
Drag arrow: the flat plate is pulled towards the trench.
Earthquake focus: the slab cracks as it bends and sinks.
Earthquake focus: deeper quakes mark the slab going down.
Earthquake focus: the deepest quakes sit furthest along the slab.

steps.text: The sinking slab pulls the whole plate behind it — slab-pull

scenes.caption: Magma rises and builds a volcanic arc
scenes.narration: Deep down, the slab heats up and releases water that melts the mantle above it. The magma rises through the overriding plate and erupts, building a curved line of volcanoes — a volcanic arc — parallel to the trench. And nobody pushed the plate down: it sank and pulled.

shape.explain: Mantle: melted just above the deep slab, feeding the volcanoes.
Ocean: the arc rises on the far side of the trench.
Continental plate: magma rises through it to build the arc.
The slab: the same sinking plate that causes the trench and the quakes.
Trailing oceanic plate: dragged in behind the slab.
Volcano: built up layer by layer where magma reaches the surface.

shape.text: A volcanic arc above the slab
shape.explain: Label: the volcanic arc, parallel to the trench.
Magma blob: molten rock rising from above the deep slab.
Magma blob: more melt following the same path up.
Eruption: magma reaches the surface and the arc grows.

steps.text: One chain: slab sinks and pulls — trench, earthquakes, volcanic arc
